title: Ephemeral connection hedging and priority drain policy for active-active edge
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Context: Hosted API traffic is active-active across regions. We see transient tail-latency and connection stalls during region-level degradations which disproportionately affect streaming and sessionful clients. This ticket proposes two coordinated controls: 1) ephemeral connection hedging at the gateway for slow initial handshake/first-token stalls, and 2) a priority-based drain policy for graceful migration of streaming sessions during regional capacity outages. Both controls must be SLO-aware, integrate with circuit-breakers and load-shedding policies, and preserve KV cache continuity where possible.
problem_statement: In partial-region degradation or noisy neighbor scenarios, some edge gateways experience long TTFB or connection jitter. Streaming clients (server-sent events / WebSocket-like long-lived streams) either stall or are dropped when we fail over traffic. Existing failover frequently triggers abrupt session terminations or broad shedding that violates 99% tail SLOs for streaming continuations. We need a mechanism to reduce impact on active streams while keeping the platform resilient and cost-predictable.
proposed_solution: 1) Ephemeral hedging: when a new connection or stream handshake exceeds a small RTT threshold (configurable per region/route), the gateway launches a speculative parallel attempt to a sibling region or to a warm standby node. The first successful handshake wins; the other is cancelled. Hedging is capped per-client and per-gateway to avoid amplification and is disabled for known idempotency-risk endpoints unless explicitly allowed. 2) Priority drain policy: define session priority buckets (real-time, interactive, background) and a graceful drain algorithm that first diverts new connections away from the impacted region, then migrates low-priority existing sessions by issuing a drain signal with KV snapshot and reconnect guidance. High-priority sessions are preserved via temporary burst capacity or routed to fallback model variants. Hedging and drain decisions are SLO-aware (respect per-route latency and continuation SLOs) and integrated with circuit-breaker states so hedging doesn't cause cascading load on fallback regions.
design_notes:
- Handshake hedging should be implemented inside the gateway proxy (e.g., envoy filter or internal proxy layer) so it is transparent to SDKs.
- Use a token-level correlation id to ensure only the winner proceeds to full session establishment; the loser returns a controlled rejection or cancellation code.
- KV snapshot: lightweight, incremental prefix snapshot pushed to the target region before switching streaming continuation. For large client state, fall back to reconnect-and-sync semantics.
- Circuit-breaker integration: hedging is allowed only when target region circuit-breaker is CLOSED or HALF-OPEN. If a region is OPEN, it's excluded from hedging targets.
- Rate limiting: global quota to ensure hedging does not double traffic unexpectedly. Hedging budget consumes a separate "hedge_units" token in throttling accounting to make cost visible in billing dashboards.
tradeoffs:
- Pros: reduces first-byte stalls, improves streaming continuity, smoother user experience.
- Cons: higher short-term resource usage (duplicate handshakes), additional complexity in cross-region state sync, potential for increased egress/billing.
- Risk: If not carefully rate-limited, hedging could amplify load onto healthy regions during a cascading incident. Mitigation: strict per-gateway caps and telemetry-driven automatic disablement when aggregate hedging error rate rises.
acceptance_criteria: H1: New-stream hedging reduces initial handshake 95th percentile TTFB by >=30% in synthetic regional-degradation tests.

H2: During a simulated region outage, >95% of high-priority streams remain connected (either via direct continuation or seamless reconnect with KV sync) and 99% of connection drops are recoverable within the session SLO window.
H3: Hedging budget metrics appear in Console with per-route cost impact and can be disabled via a runtime flag.
H4: No increase in error budget burn for non-target routes beyond 5% during canary rollout.
H5: Runbook updated and on-call run-through completed with incident simulation.
H6: Automated integration tests for hedging and drain policy added to cicd/edge-integration-suite.
tasks: T1: Implement hedging decision layer in gateway proxy with configurable RTT threshold and target-selection algorithm.
T2: Add hedging quota counters and billing metric emission (hedge_units).
T3: Implement priority buckets and drain RPC in session coordinator; KV snapshot API extension for incremental prefixes.
T4: Integrate hedging logic with circuit-breaker state and load-shed controller.
T5: End-to-end tests: synthetic latency injector, regional outage simulator, streaming continuity verification.
T6: Console dashboard: hedging usage, regional failure correlation, per-route SLO impact visualization.
T7: Security review for handshake duplication semantics and telemetry privacy.
T8: Canary rollout to 5% of edge traffic, monitor metrics, and iterate.
T9: Update runbooks and on-call playbook for active-active handoff with hedging enabled.
telemetry: metric:edge.hedge.attempts - count of hedging attempts per route/region
metric:edge.hedge.success_rate - fraction where hedged connection produced successful handshake first
metric:edge.hedge.latency_delta_ms - TTFB improvement when hedging fired
metric:edge.drain.sessions_migrated - number of sessions migrated by priority bucket
metric:edge.kv.snapshot.size_bytes - avg KV snapshot size per migration
trace:handoff.correlation_id - end-to-end trace for migrated sessions
dashboard panels: hedging cost impact, number of duplicate handshakes, per-route SLO burn vs hedging activity
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Labs: Implement feature behind runtime flag and run internal lab against noisy neighbor testbed.
Phase 1 - Canary: 5% production traffic, hedging budget capped; observe hedging.success_rate and edge.drain.sessions_migrated for 72 hours.
Phase 2 - Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 50% with automated checks; if hedging error rate > 2% or extra SLO burn > 5% rollback immediate.
Phase 3 - Regional opt-in: enable per-region hedging if telemetry indicates benefit per-region.
Phase 4 - Full enablement: expose configuration to Dedicated/private customers and Console toggles.
Rollback criteria: sustained increase in downstream CPU by >20% attributable to hedging, hedging error rate >2%, or unexplainable SLO burn >5% for 1 hour.
test_plan: Unit tests for hedging decision matrix and quota accounting.
Integration test: two-region handshake simulator with artificial RTT jitter and packet loss.
Chaos test: introduce cascading load into fallback region to ensure hedging disables automatically and circuit-breakers trip as expected.
Load test: ensure hedging budget enforcement prevents amplification at 10k RPS gateway scale.
End-to-end: streaming client reconnect with KV incremental sync validates state continuity within 3s resume SLO.
Manual runbook drill: on-call performs region outage simulation and validates procedures.
notes: PM sync 2026-03-02: Product asked for explicit billing signal for hedging due to customer cost sensitivity.

Engineering note: start with handshake hedging only; postpone full-stream state handoff until KV incremental snapshot is stable.
